newsitem.title: UK: Unilever shares jump after 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: Unilever shares jump after 1996 results.

text.p: Shares in Unilever Plc jumped in pre-market trade on Tuesday after the company announced higher-than-expected 1996 profits and said it was selling its speciality chemicals businesses
Unilever shares were 47p higher at 14.40 stg by 0803 GMT.
The Anglo-Dutch food-to-detergents conglomerate reported annual pre-tax profits of 2.66 billion stg compared with an average forecast among 24 brokers polled of 2.53 billion.
"Looking ahead, the overall economic situation in 1997 is likely to be reasonably similar to 1996, generally favourable," Unilever chairman Niall FitzGerald said.
The company said it was selling its speciality chemicals businesses as part of the strategic development of its portfolio.
"Profits were better than people were expecting and they were also fairly bullish on next year," one market-maker said.
"Selling their chemicals businesses seems to have been taken well, and overall people have been pleasantly surprised and the shares are roaring up," he added.

Other food and consumer products groups were boosted by the results. Reckitt and Colman shares climbed 21-1/2p to 731 while Cadbury Schweppes Plc firmed nine pence to 486 and Associated British Foods Plc rose 10-1/2p to 491-1/2.
